metadata.title: Breaking Food Stereotype | Eri Silkworm
metadata.description:
Humans for thousands of years have harvested, the eggs, larvae, pupae and adult of certain insect species for consumption as regular diet, for medicinal purpose and as a novelty food item. The practice of human consumption of insect is known as Entomophagy. 

Insects contain more protein than equal amount of beef or fish and have very high calorific value than meats, corn or lentils. 
About 255 species of edible insects have been recorded from various parts of India. The tribes of Arunachal Pradesh consume the highest number of insects, a total of 158 recorded species. Followed by Assam, Manipur and Nagaland (16 – 40 species), to a lesser extent in Meghalaya i.e about 16 species. 
In the southern and central part of India, the local population consume most the winged termites, except for Kerala where a total of 6 species of insects are consumed.
Entomophagy can actually be instrumental in combating malnutrition and strengthen the food security system. In a recently held international workshop sponsored by the United nations Food and Agriculture Organization titled “Forest Insects as Food – Humans bite back” Considered insects as a natural food source and emphasised on development of insects as food and feed to combat food insecurity.
